related_links.title: Friday Games To Watch: November 6 varsity preview

article.headline: Scores from last Night: Jackson Prep reaches MAIS final; Eupora ousts Bruce
article.html:
Jackson Prep earned a place in the MAIS Class 4A Division I final Friday, November 6, defeating Jackson Academy 42-21. In the MHSAA playoffs, Eupora ended Bruce’s season with a 38-20 road win, while Corinth and Kossuth advanced with decisive home victories.

Away from football, Meridian swept its basketball games at Starkville, Brandon and Northwest Rankin won girls soccer meetings between unbeaten teams, and Center Hill and DeSoto Central split penalty-shootout decisions. Several of the matchups were featured in our Friday Games To Watch preview.

Football: Jackson Prep books a place in the final

Jackson Prep beat visiting Jackson Academy 42-21 to improve to 11-1, leaving the Raiders at 8-3. The Patriots outscored JA 21-7 in the third quarter and 14-7 in the fourth. The MAIS bracket places Prep in the November 13 championship game.

Heritage Academy also found a way through a close playoff game, beating Washington of Greenville 24-21 in Columbus. The Patriots were listed at 4-7 after the win, while Washington finished 8-4.

Football: Eupora knocks out Bruce

Eupora won 38-20 at Bruce in the Class 2A first round. Both teams were listed at 9-2 afterward, but the Eagles move on while the Trojans are eliminated. The updated bracket pairs Eupora with Charleston on November 13.

Football: Corinth and Kosciusko set up a second-round meeting

Corinth shut out Ripley 42-0, scoring 14 points in each of the first three quarters. The Warriors reached 7-3 and held the Tigers scoreless throughout their Class 4A opener. Ripley finished 2-9.

Kosciusko defeated Itawamba Agricultural 48-21, scoring 20 points in the fourth quarter to finish the night 10-1. The Indians were listed at 6-3. Those wins put Corinth and Kosciusko together in the November 13 second round.

Football: Kossuth advances; other county and Tippah teams fall

Kossuth beat Amanda Elzy 38-6 in Class 3A. The Aggies kept the Panthers off the scoreboard through three quarters and reached 7-3; Elzy finished 3-8. The second-round bracket pairs Kossuth with Winona on November 13.

Alcorn Central lost 42-13 at O’Bannon, ending 5-6 while the Greenwaves reached 9-1. Biggersville lost 34-14 at Okolona in Class 1A, finishing 2-8; the Chieftains moved to 6-5.

French Camp Academy won 55-14 at Falkner in the Class 1A first round. The Panthers reached 4-7, and the Eagles finished 5-5. In Class 2A, North Side beat visiting Walnut 48-6, leaving the Gators 8-2 and the Wildcats 4-7.

Basketball: Meridian sweeps at Starkville

Meridian boys won 55-49 at the school that won the 2026 boys Class 7A title. The Wildcats reached 2-0 and Starkville stood at 0-1. Meridian girls won 54-35, with the Wildcats listed at 2-0 and the Yellowjackets at 0-1 afterward.

Hernando boys held off Oxford 63-60 at home. The Tigers moved to 2-0, while the Chargers were listed at 0-1.

Center Hill won both basketball games at Holly Springs. The boys took a 56-43 win to reach 2-0. The girls won 47-35 for their first victory, leaving the Mustangs 1-1. Both Holly Springs teams were listed at 0-2.

Girls soccer: Brandon and Northwest Rankin end unbeaten starts

Brandon beat Oxford 4-2, moving to 4-0 and handing the Chargers their first loss at 2-1. The teams were tied 1-1 at halftime before the Bulldogs outscored Oxford 3-1 in the second half.

Northwest Rankin defeated Sumrall 4-1. The Cougars reached 2-0, while the Bobcats’ first loss left them 5-1. Both girls soccer games changed the unbeaten-record comparisons highlighted in Friday’s preview.

Soccer: Center Hill and DeSoto Central split shootouts

Center Hill girls won the penalty shootout 4-3 after a 3-3 finish against DeSoto Central. The Mustangs were listed at 2-0 and the Jaguars at 1-4 after the decision.

The boys game finished 1-1 before penalties, with DeSoto Central winning the shootout, as DeSoto County News confirms. DeSoto Central was listed at 2-1-1 afterward, and Center Hill at 2-1. The available report does not give the boys shootout tally.

facts.claim: Eupora defeated Bruce 38-20 and North Side defeated Walnut 48-6 in Class 2A first-round playoff games on November 6.

evidence.excerpt: 2A Location Various Cities, MS When two teams from the same region meet in the football playoffs, the higher seed will always be the home team, no matter what round. Class 1A, 2A, 3A, 4A 1. First and second round – higher seed hosts. 2. Third round – If both teams have played an equal number of home matches the home site will be determined by the highest seeded team. If equally seeded teams play and #2 cannot determine a home site, the HIGHER number of opponent’s region for the season will be the home team. 3. North/South Championships – highest seed hosts. If equally seeded teams, the HIGHER numbered region will host. 4. State Championships North team will be home.
